5556.text: In Ezek.20.40 'require' shifts to the base sense 'to seek (with a demand), demand, require' (1a4) applied to cultic contributions/gifts - a distinctly legal-cultic exaction nuance compared to the devotional-seeking sense dominant elsewhere in the arc (e.g. Ps.119.155, 2Chr.30.19); here the impact is to frame God's acceptance of Israel's worship as itself an act of formally demanding their offerings, intensifying the transactional-covenantal register of the verse.

5560.text: In Ezek.20.40, the operation 'require' (H1875) is initiated by the Lord God (T7-tagged party) and directed toward the house of Israel (T11-tagged party), demanding their contributions and offerings - a divine-to-covenant-people exaction operation.

5564.text: In Ezek.20.40, H1875 (require) co-occurs with M61 (holy/sacred offerings), M08 (height), M42 (declares), M36 (serve), M39 (accept); this characteristic's vantage: 'require' is the concluding transactional act that formally claims the sacred contributions (M61) after acceptance (M39) of the people's service (M36), closing the covenantal exchange sequence.

5576.text: In Ezek.20.40 'height' functions as a qualifier of 'mountain' (the mountain height of Israel), specifying the elevated topographical status of the sanctuary-mountain rather than naming an independent quality; a modifying rather than standalone use.

14966.text: The passage. The Rabshakeh's speech has been heard (2Ki 18). Hezekiah "tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of the Lord" (19:1). His message: "This day is a day of distress, of rebuke, and of disgrace" (19:3). Isaiah answers: "Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have reviled me" (19:6). A letter comes; Hezekiah "spread it before the Lord" and prays (19:14–19). The Lord answers with an oracle against Sennacherib (19:21–28), and the camp is struck (19:35). 2Ch 32 tells the same campaign with the purpose of the shouting stated (32:18) and the end: "he returned with shame of face to his own land" (32:21).

14975.text: Sennacherib as a passage. Mockery of God sent through servants, letters and shouting; its stated aim is to make the hearers afraid (2Ch 32:18). Hezekiah's response: sackcloth, the house of the Lord, the letter spread before God, prayer (2Ki 19:1, 14–19). God's word to the people: "Do not be afraid" (19:6). God names himself as the one mocked (19:22), knows the mocker's raging (19:27), turns the scorn back (19:21), and the mocker goes home with shame of face (2Ch 32:21). Hezekiah calls the day one "of disgrace" (2Ki 19:3, a contempt word, M06).

15113.text: The heart rises out of what it has been given. This is the clearest single pattern in the batch, and the verses state it each time: Strength. Uzziah "was marvelously helped, till he was strong. But when he was strong, he grew proud, to his destruction" (2Ch 26:15–16); Healing and honour. Hezekiah was healed, given a sign, and "exalted in the sight of all nations". Then: "But Hezekiah did not make return according to the benefit done to him, for his heart was proud" (2Ch 32:23–25). Here pride is a failure to return what was received. It was humbled the next verse (32:26, carried from M09); Greatness and majesty. "the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father kingship and greatness and glory and majesty ... But when his heart was lifted up and his spirit was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was brought down" (Dan 5:18–20). It lasted "until he knew that the Most High God rules the kingdom of mankind" (5:21); Wealth. "by your great wisdom in your trade you have increased your wealth, and your heart has become proud in your wealth" (Eze 28:5); Beauty. "You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created, till unrighteousness was found in you ... Your heart was proud because of your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendor" (Eze 28:15–17); Height. The cedar God made beautiful ("I made it beautiful", Eze 31:9): "its heart was proud of its height" (31:10).

15115.text: Pride deceives the one who has it: "The pride of your heart has deceived you ... who say in your heart, 'Who will bring me down to the ground?'" (Obd 3); "Though you soar aloft like the eagle ... from there I will bring you down" (Obd 4); Jer 49:16 adds a second deceiver: "The horror you inspire has deceived you, and the pride of your heart". The fear others feel feeds the self-deception.

15237.text: A pride word is used of God here. lāʿag "mock" and lîṣ "scorn" are said of God: "the Lord holds them in derision" (Psa 2:4); "you hold all the nations in derision" (Psa 59:8); "Toward the scorners he is scornful" (Pro 3:34); wisdom: "I will mock when terror strikes you" (Pro 1:26); The verses show how God's derision differs from human mocking; Where it comes from. It comes from the one who "sits in the heavens" (Psa 2:4), from the height that batches 1–3 found is his by nature; What it answers. It always answers a rising against him: kings set "against the Lord and against his Anointed" (Psa 2:2), those of whom it says "'Who,' they think, 'will hear us?'" (Psa 59:7), the scorners (Pro 3:34), those who "refused to listen" (Pro 1:24); Whom it never targets. In these verses it is never aimed at the weak, the poor or the sufferer. Human mocking is aimed at exactly those: the poor (Pro 17:5), a father (Pro 30:17), the sufferer (Psa 22:7), builders called "feeble" (Neh 4:2); I read: God's derision is the laughter of the undisputed height at a dispute that cannot succeed. Human mockery is a self-made height looking down on someone made low; God is not mocked. "Do not be deceived: God is not mocked" (Gal 6:7). The mocking of his messengers goes on "until there was no remedy" (2Ch 36:16). This is the batch 1 point again: God's standing is challenged, and is not overturned; The Son is mocked, and does not answer in kind; The one with the undisputed standing is mocked on that very standing: "Hail, King of the Jews!" (Mat 27:29); "He saved others; he cannot save himself" (Mar 15:31); He "made no answer" (Luk 23:9), and he prays "Father, forgive them" (Luk 23:34); I read: in the Son, the majesty of batch 1 does not defend itself against mockery. This is the clearest instance of 13.1 Lowering himself in these words. It joins the batch 1 point that his majesty and his being "delivered into the hands of men" stand side by side (Luk 9:43–44); Mocking exposes a false height. Zion scorns Sennacherib (2Ki 19:21). Elijah mocks a god who does not answer (1Ki 18:27). Here the mocking does not come from pride. It names a claim that is empty.

15258.text: God's height is his own, shown in acts, and not overturned: "robed in majesty ... you are from everlasting" (Psa 93:1–2). "In the greatness of your majesty you overthrow your adversaries" (Exo 15:7); Majesty goes with what only God does: abasing every proud one and saving by his own hand (Job 40:10–14); "God is not mocked" (Gal 6:7); Human pride, in the verses' own words, is a standing taken or assumed; "you make your heart like the heart of a god" (Eze 28:2); "takes his seat in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God" (2Th 2:4); "By the strength of my hand I have done it" (Isa 10:13); "if anyone thinks he is something, when he is nothing, he deceives himself" (Gal 6:3); Mostly, pride holds as its own what was given; "What do you have that you did not receive? If then you received it, why do you boast as if you did not receive it?" (1Co 4:7); In story: Uzziah's strength, Hezekiah's healing, Nebuchadnezzar's God-given majesty, the cherub's beauty, the cedar's height (2Ch 26:15–16; 32:24–25; Dan 5:18–20; Eze 28:17; 31:9–10); This matches the researcher's "mostly assumed": the standing is real, but it is taken up as if it were not received.

15282.text: Verses with no other M-code (96). Most are height as a measure: Exo 25 to 38, 1Ki 6 to 7, Eze 40 to 42, and Goliath in 1Sa 17:4. Others are central to the cluster: Paul's boasting: Rom 15:17, Gal 6:14, 1Co 1:31, 2Co 10:17, 2Co 12:1, Eph 2:9; Jam 3:5, the tongue that "boasts of great things"; Isa 3:16, the daughters of Zion "haughty"; the mocking of Jesus: Mat 27:31, Mat 27:41, Mar 15:20, Luk 23:36; 2Ki 2:23, the boys who jeered Elisha.

15301.text: Pride is the given held as one's own: "What do you have that you did not receive? If then you received it, why do you boast as if you did not receive it?" (1Co 4:7); In story, each time:; "when he was strong, he grew proud" (2Ch 26:16); "did not make return according to the benefit done to him, for his heart was proud" (2Ch 32:25); "when his heart was lifted up" (Dan 5:20); "your heart has become proud in your wealth" (Eze 28:5); "its heart was proud of its height" (Eze 31:10); In the law it is foreseen: "your heart be lifted up, and you forget the Lord your God ... Beware lest you say in your heart, 'My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth'" (Deu 8:14, 17); It credits its own hand. "By the strength of my hand I have done it", said by the one who was the Lord's rod: "Shall the axe boast over him who hews with it" (Isa 10:13, 15). And "which I have built by my mighty power" (Dan 4:30); I read: the line the verses draw is not between having height and having none. It is the source and the direction. Height that is one's own by nature belongs to God alone. Height that is given is held from him. Pride is the given taken as one's own, and turned against the giver or over others. This is the researcher's "assumed position", in the verses' own words.

15305.text: And it deceives: "The pride of your heart has deceived you" (Obd 3); "The horror you inspire has deceived you, and the pride of your heart" (Jer 49:16).

15314.text: What it is set against, God answers otherwise: "though the Lord is high, he regards the lowly, but the haughty he knows from afar" (Psa 138:6); God's derision answers only those who rise against him (Psa 2:2–4; 59:7–8; Pro 1:24–26; 3:34). In these verses it is never aimed at the weak.

15358.text: Isa 26:5–6: "he has humbled the inhabitants of the height, the lofty city … The foot tramples it, the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy." The proud city brought low is walked on by the poor. It sits beside "You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you" (26:3).

15702.text: H7806 (shazar, 19 verses, the family's single largest strong) is glossed to twist, but every one of its 19 citations is literal tabernacle-construction material, fine twined linen repeated almost verbatim through Exodus 26 to 39 (curtains, the ephod, the breastpiece, the veil). It is technical textile vocabulary, not moral language at all; with the chul codes it accounts for 28 of the family's about 98 verses, a gloss-text-grouping failure of the same kind as family R and G0073.

15805.text: H7806 (shazar, to twist) has real, coherent meaning: a technical textile-craft term. All 19 occurrences are the tabernacle-construction formula fine twined linen, repeated near-verbatim through Exodus 26 to 39 (curtains, the ephod, the breastpiece, the veil, the screen). 15823.text: In Isa 57:15 and 1 Sam 16:7, both marked by the M08 strand's group B scan, the height word is not pride: it supports M47 (heart, spirit). 16211.text: 16.10 Life risked "to death" for others — the OT precedent: "Zebulun is a people who risked their lives to the death" (Judg 5:18). This is in the same song as "March on, my soul, with might!" (5:21; §3.2).; "Our life for yours even to death!" (Jos 2:14; §4 revisit); David "took his life in his hand" against the Philistine (1Sa 19:5); The men to David: "If half of us die, they will not care [*set heart*] about us. But you are worth ten thousand of us" (2Sa 18:3). The enemy's heart is indifferent to many deaths. One life is weighed at ten thousand.; "the men who were seeking your life are dead" (Exo 4:19) → Moses returns (4:20). The death of the hunters frees the hunted life.; "Why then are you laying a trap for my life to bring about my death?" (1Sa 28:9). This is the medium to the disguised Saul.; "we are about to bring great disaster upon ourselves [*our souls*]" (Jer 26:19). To put the prophet to death would harm the souls of those who kill him. It is set against Hezekiah, who "feared the Lord … and the Lord relented".; [Claude reading] Batch F §3.2 read "hating one's life" and "not loving one's life unto death" as NT discipleship. The OT already has the same shape in battle and in covenant pledges: the life risked "to the death" for a people, a household or a king. What the NT adds is the object, "for the name of the Lord Jesus" (Act 21:13), and the example, "poured out his soul to death" (Isa 53:12).

16727.text: 11. Cross-cutting observations for Batch D [Claude reading]: Conscience is the NT's named moral-awareness faculty. It can be clear, pure, good, evil, defiled, seared, weak or wounded. It testifies (2Co 1:12; Rom 9:1) and is purified by Christ's blood (Heb 9:14). It is frequently paired with the heart (1Ti 1:5; Heb 10:22).; The OT does this work with the heart: "David's heart struck him" (2Sa 24:10); "my heart does not reproach me" (Job 27:6).; The Levitical "realizes his guilt" (Lev 5) describes the same moment without naming an organ.; The heart deceives itself and is the source of evil.; It deceives its owner: Jer 17:9; Obd 3; Isa 44:20.; Evil comes from it: Gen 6:5; Mat 15:19; Luk 6:45.; Its evil hides behind speech: Psa 28:3; 41:6; Pro 26:23–25.; Pride deceives the heart that holds it (Obd 3), linking M08 and M14.; Flesh carries on from Batch C (§11.5).; OT: flesh is the ritual body and meat — clean or unclean, holy or tainted.; NT Pauline: flesh is the seat of sin (Rom 7–8; Gal 5:19) and the ground of false boasting (Phili 3:3).; Positive NT uses remain: "holy … in his body of flesh" (Col 1:22); "bodies as a living sacrifice" (Rom 12:1).; Wind and breath are the image of moral emptiness: iniquity takes us away like wind (Isa 64:6); the wicked are chaff (Psa 1:4); "wind and lies" (Mic 2:11); idols with no breath (Jer 10:14); the *hevel* + *rûaḥ* refrain (Ecc); Only the messianic "breath of his lips" (Isa 11:4) and the breath that conveys the Holy Spirit (Joh 20:22) are active and effective.; Fringe worth keeping: *nephesh* = corpse as the defiling body (§8.2); the "high heart" that is pride or courage depending on direction (2Ch 17:6 vs 2Ch 32:25); the heart that strikes or does not reproach — pre-conscience (§3.3, §9.5); sin against one's own soul (§3.2); the servant's soul as guilt offering (§3.6); lies that kill and keep alive souls (Eze 13:19); the spirit of jealousy that comes whether or not the defilement is real (Num 5:14); false humility of the flesh (Col 2:18, 23); the thorn in the flesh against conceit (2Co 12:7); Eliab misreading David's heart (1Sa 17:28); "Is your heart true to my heart as mine is to yours?" (2Ki 10:15)

To God it is a stream in his hand.

17274.text: 3.4 Distinction — where the text separates the components: *Division of soul and spirit (Heb 4:12):* "piercing to the division of soul and of spirit, of joints and of marrow, and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart." [Claude reading] Soul and spirit are close enough that only the word of God can separate them, just as joints and marrow are adjacent parts of the body. The heart is where the *thoughts and intentions* are, and they are *discerned* there.; *Living soul vs life-giving spirit:* "The first man Adam became a living being [psychē]; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit" (1Co 15:45; cf. Gen 2:7).; *Spirit vs mind:* 1Co 14:14–15 (above).; *Spirit vs flesh (as kind):*; "a spirit does not have flesh and bones" (Luk 24:39); "horses are flesh, and not spirit" (Isa 31:3); "That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit" (Joh 3:6); "the flesh is no help at all" (Joh 6:63); "put to death in the flesh but made alive in the spirit" (1Pe 3:18; 4:6); "the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved" (1Co 5:5); *Soul vs body:* "cannot kill the soul" (Mat 10:28).; *Spirit vs body in place:* "absent in body, … present in spirit" (1Co 5:3–4; Col 2:5). fringe [Claude reading]: the spirit can be "with" people where the body is not.; *Inner vs outer:*; "Though our outer self is wasting away, our inner self is being renewed day by day" (2Co 4:16, with "lose heart"); "a Jew is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit" (Rom 2:29); "the hidden person of the heart with the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit" (1Pe 3:4); "man looks on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart" (1Sa 16:7); "what is in the heart" vs "outward appearance" (2Co 5:12); *Food and the heart:* "since it enters not his heart but his stomach, and is expelled" (Mar 7:19). The text draws a boundary: food goes to the stomach, not the heart. But see §3.6, where food *does* strengthen the heart.

17279.text: 3.8 The inner seat shared or joined between persons ◆ fringe cluster: *Soul to soul:*; "the soul of Jonathan was knit to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul" (1Sa 18:1, 3; 20:17); "your friend who is as your own soul" (Deu 13:6, with "the wife you embrace"); "his life is bound up in the boy's life" (Gen 44:30); *Heart to heart:* "my heart will be joined to you" (1Ch 12:17); "Is your heart true to my heart as mine is to yours?" (2Ki 10:15); "you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together" (2Co 7:3); "I hold you in my heart" (Phili 1:7); "in person not in heart" (1Th 2:17).; *Shared across a group:* "one heart and soul" (Act 4:32); "one spirit, with one mind" (Phili 1:27); "Did we not act in the same spirit?" (2Co 12:18).; *Transferred between persons:* "a double portion of your spirit" (2Ki 2:9, 15); "take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them" (Num 11:17, 25); "in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children" (Luk 1:17; Mal 4:6).; *Captured or stolen by others:* "Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel" (2Sa 15:6); "his wives turned away his heart" (1Ki 11:3); "he swayed the heart of all the men of Judah as one man" (2Sa 19:14).; *Known from shared experience:* "You know the heart [nephesh] of a sojourner, for you were sojourners" (Exo 23:9).; *With a spouse:* "guard yourselves in your spirit, and let none of you be faithless to the wife of your youth" (Mal 2:15–16); "one flesh" (Gen 2:24).; [Claude reading] The inner seat is not depicted as sealed inside the individual. It can be knit to, joined with, held within, carried in, stolen by, or shared with another person. It can also be passed from one person to another (spirit).

Each still needs reading for its will word.

20210.text: Heb 6:17 is in both sets. God *"desired"* (will) to show the unchangeable character of *"his purpose"* (plan).

20224.text: A (other beings) — 21 verses: Deu 10:10; 23:5; 29:20; Jos 24:10; 2Ki 8:19; 13:23; 24:4; 2Ch 21:7; Dan 4:17, 25, 32, 35; 5:21; Mat 11:27; Luk 10:22; Rom 9:19; 1Co 12:11; Heb 6:17; Jam 1:18; 2Pe 3:9; Luk 22:42.; Also B: Deu 10:10 (Moses' intercession), Deu 29:20 (the self-blessing heart), Dan 4:25 and 4:32 (the king's learning), Dan 5:21, Luk 22:42.

20228.text: Colossians 3:12: "Put on then, as God's chosen ones … compassionate hearts": The chapter begins with where the chosen now stand: *"If then you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above"* (v1); *"Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth"* (v2); *"your life is hidden with Christ in God"* (v3).; Then it tells them what to put away: *"Put to death therefore what is earthly in you: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry"* (v5); *"But now you must put them all away: anger, wrath, malice, slander, and obscene talk from your mouth"* (v8); They have *"put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge after the image of its creator"* (v10).; The verse comes next: *"Put on then, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience"* (v12). "Compassionate hearts" is literally the inward parts (G4698) of compassion. The verse gives being chosen as the ground ("as God's chosen ones"), and then gives a command. The qualities are not described as already there. They are to be put on, as clothing is.; The chosen are called *"holy and beloved"*. The holiness that is the purpose of the choosing in Ephesians 1:4 is here a name the chosen already carry, and the inner qualities are still to be put on. I set the two letters side by side; neither refers to the other.; What the chosen put on is turned toward one another: *"bearing with one another and, if one has a complaint against another, forgiving each other; as the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive"* (v13); *"And above all these put on love, which binds everything together in perfect harmony"* (v14); *"And let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to which indeed you were called in one body. And be thankful"* (v15); The forgiving is measured by being forgiven. The peace is to rule in the heart.

20229.text: 2 Thessalonians 2:13: "God chose you … through sanctification by the Spirit and belief in the truth": The chapter is about deception. Paul asks them *"not to be quickly shaken in mind or alarmed"* (v2), and warns *"Let no one deceive you in any way"* (v3). The lawless one comes *"with all wicked deception for those who are perishing"* (v10).; Before the choosing verse, the passage names the inner state of those who perish: *"because they refused to love the truth and so be saved"* (v10); *"Therefore God sends them a strong delusion, so that they may believe what is false"* (v11); *"in order that all may be condemned who did not believe the truth but had pleasure in unrighteousness"* (v12); Then: *"But we ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers beloved by the Lord, because God chose you as the firstfruits to be saved, through sanctification by the Spirit and belief in the truth"* (v13). "Belief" in v13 and "believe" in v12 are the same root (G4102, G4100), and "truth" is the same word in v10, v12 and v13 (G0225). The chosen are set against the perishing in the passage's own words. The perishing did not believe the truth. The chosen are saved *"through … belief in the truth"*. The perishing had pleasure in unrighteousness. The chosen are sanctified *"by the Spirit"*.; In the verse, God's choosing and the person's belief stand in one sentence. The verse does not say which comes first, or how they fit.; The passage then gives the chosen two things to do, and asks for one thing to be done in them: *"To this he called you through our gospel, so that you may obtain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ"* (v14); *"So then, brothers, stand firm and hold to the traditions that you were taught by us"* (v15); *"comfort your hearts and establish them in every good work and word"* (v17), asked of the Lord Jesus Christ and of God the Father, *"who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace"* (v16)

20230.text: Titus 1:1: "for the sake of the faith of God's elect and their knowledge of the truth, which accords with godliness": Paul opens by saying what his own service is for: *"for the sake of the faith of God's elect and their knowledge of the truth, which accords with godliness, in hope of eternal life, which God, who never lies, promised before the ages began"* (v1–2). Faith, knowledge of the truth, godliness and hope are named as belonging to the elect, and his work serves them.; The rest of the chapter is about who may lead them. The overseer's inner life is set out in full: *"He must not be arrogant or quick-tempered or a drunkard or violent or greedy for gain"* (v7); *"but hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined"* (v8); *"He must hold firm to the trustworthy word as taught"* (v9); Against the elect's knowledge of the truth, the chapter sets those who teach otherwise: *"not devoting themselves to Jewish myths and the commands of people who turn away from the truth"* (v14); *"to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both their minds and their consciences are defiled"* (v15); *"They profess to know God, but they deny him by their works"* (v16); The elect's knowledge of the truth *"accords with godliness"*. The others say they know God and deny him by what they do. The chapter sets the two side by side.

20231.text: James 2:5: "has not God chosen those who are poor in the world to be rich in faith": The setting is an assembly that chooses where people sit: *"if you pay attention to the one who wears the fine clothing and say, 'You sit here in a good place,' while you say to the poor man, 'You stand over there'"* (v3). James names what that shows of them inside: *"have you not then made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?"* (v4).; He answers their way of choosing with God's: *"Listen, my beloved brothers, has not God chosen those who are poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, which he has promised to those who love him?"* (v5). The poor man they sent to stand is the kind of man God chose. The assembly went by clothing. God's choice goes by something else, and its aim is that the poor be *"rich in faith"*.; The promise is to *"those who love him"*. The love here is the chosen people's love for God.; Then: *"But you have dishonored the poor man"* (v6). Choosing against God's choice is a sin: *"if you show partiality, you are committing sin"* (v9).; The faith of the chosen poor is then tested by what it does: *"What good is it, my brothers, if someone says he has faith but does not have works?"* (v14); *"So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead"* (v17); Abraham: *"faith was active along with his works, and faith was completed by his works … and he was called a friend of God"* (v22–23)

20234.text: Revelation 17:14: "those with him are called and chosen and faithful": The chapter is a vision of judgment on *"the great prostitute"*, with whom *"the dwellers on earth have become drunk"* (v2). The seer himself is moved: *"When I saw her, I marveled greatly"* (v6). He is asked *"Why do you marvel?"* (v7). Those who marvel at the beast are *"the dwellers on earth whose names have not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world"* (v8). The vision *"calls for a mind with wisdom"* (v9).; The kings who serve the beast are of one mind: *"These are of one mind, and they hand over their power and authority to the beast"* (v13). Then: *"They will make war on the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, for he is Lord of lords and King of kings, and those with him are called and chosen and faithful"* (v14).; The chosen are named by three words, and the third is about them: *"faithful"*. They are *"with him"*. The verse says nothing more of their inner life.; The chapter says this of the kings: *"for God has put it into their hearts to carry out his purpose by being of one mind and handing over their royal power to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled"* (v17). "Mind" in v13 and "purpose" in v17 are the same word (G1106): the kings' one mind is God's purpose carried out. This is God acting on the hearts of others, not on the chosen. It belongs with 13.1 more than here.

20289.text: 2 Timothy 2:10: "Therefore I endure everything for the sake of the elect": Paul writes from chains: *"my gospel, for which I am suffering, bound with chains as a criminal. But the word of God is not bound!"* (v8–9). Then: *"Therefore I endure everything for the sake of the elect, that they also may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory"* (v10).; "Endure" is *hupomenō* (G5278). The same word comes in the saying that follows: *"if we endure, we will also reign with him"* (v12). The endurance is Paul's. It is for others, the elect, and for their salvation.; The same passage calls Timothy to it: *"Share in suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus"* (v3). It gives the ground: *"if we are faithless, he remains faithful—for he cannot deny himself"* (v13).

21316.text: Called is here a public proclamation, summons or announcement to others; it is the outward act and bears on the hearers, with no inner-being operation of the caller named.
